### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**3** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **69** of **252** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **183** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **183**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **124** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **30** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 93fa9118a3dc61473890eafc6bb170a6fc1c3042` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `95fe84f819d7f30defbf5a792561967b7589f50d` — the merge of head `40c5c821495c1c02e2a7a4a96244fd1bc0ab1870` into base `93fa9118a3dc61473890eafc6bb170a6fc1c3042`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 95fe84f819d7f30defbf5a792561967b7589f50d && git checkout 95fe84f819d7f30defbf5a792561967b7589f50d
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 93fa9118a3dc61473890eafc6bb170a6fc1c3042 40c5c821495c1c02e2a7a4a96244fd1bc0ab1870 && git checkout -B drift-repro 93fa9118a3dc61473890eafc6bb170a6fc1c3042 && git merge --no-ff 40c5c821495c1c02e2a7a4a96244fd1bc0ab1870

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 93fa9118a3dc61473890eafc6bb170a6fc1c3042
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `40c5c821495c1c02e2a7a4a96244fd1bc0ab1870`
Local-runs: none

### ① Derived judgments

- Face: declaration only. The diff has no `packages/spec/src/**` file and no governed path; the body and changeset carry `Clause-②: yes (widening)` and `Metadata-protocol: none`, so the review owed is this one, at `TIER_DEFAULT`.
- Runtime: `executeDeclarativeUpdateAction` reads `warnings` off the data-plane update answer through `writeAnswerWarnings` (a non-empty array or `undefined`) and spreads it onto `DeclarativeUpdateResult` only when present. A write that trips no rule answers byte-for-byte as before. The stale roll-up path throws `withEarnedAnswer(stale, { ...result })` after the spread, so it carries the same member. Both doors (REST action route, MCP `run_action`) go through this executor, and the runtime suite pins each, plus the no-warnings control.
- Console: `updateAnswerWarningLines` is read only for `isUpdateOperationAction`, from `readActionPayload(result.data)`, so a script action's own `warnings` key is never read as one (reverse pin in the suite). Distinct messages, in answer order.
- Double-toast check: the action route goes through `createServerActionHandler` over the console's plain authenticated `fetch` (`consoleServerAction.ts`, `apiActionDoor.ts`), never the ObjectStack adapter's `create`/`update`, so the adapter's `emitWriteWarning` channel does not fire for an action write. The new runner toast is the only one.
- Design point (the success toast off, or a result dialog): the warning still shows on its own, titled with the rule's own message and no runner text. Agreed. A warning is the rule author's demand on the person, not success copy, and `showOnSuccess: false` turns off the success message only; it matches the record-save path, which shows the warning whatever the form's own toast settings are. `result.silent` still suppresses both, which is right for a programmatic run.
- Hosts: `useConsoleActionRuntime.tsx` and `RecordDetailView.tsx` now route `type: 'warning'` to `toast.warning` with the description and the same Undo action; both suites pin it down to `sonner`. The `@object-ui/react` hosts (`ActionContext.tsx`, `useActionRunner.ts`) pass the consumer's `onToast` through unchanged; `'warning'` was already in the `type` union, and `description` is an optional addition a consumer may ignore.
- Card #37867: all three acceptance lines are delivered (the answer carries the data door's `warnings` in its own shape; the console shows them; a test covers a write that trips a `severity: 'warning'` rule). `Fixes` is right. The `notice` and `droppedFields` drops the dev found in the same executor are out of the card, and the seat files them.

### ② Semver level

patch for `@objectstack/runtime` and `@object-ui/core`: one optional member on the action answer and one optional member on the `ToastHandler` options, nothing refused or narrowed. The `@object-ui/app-shell` entry is on a private package and changes nothing published.

### ③ Boundary flags

- The dev's surface amendment (the two app-shell host test files) is in the diff and reported to the seat; it pins the host arms and adds nothing to the contract.
- SQL push-down: no query, id materialisation or in-app join is added; not applicable.
- nit: `info`-severity hits also ride the `warning` variant. The data door answers them in the same `warnings` list and the record-save path shows them the same way, so this is consistent; no change asked.
- nit: the ObjectQL fallback arm of `callData` answers no `warnings`, so an install without the protocol slot still shows only the success toast. The JSDoc on `writeAnswerWarnings` says so; it is the pre-existing shape of that arm, not a regression.
